rationale: Both read the same distances from the diagram and find the minimum of 13. A correctly lists and sums all 24 directed paths, so its search is complete. B says it checks the 12 unique paths up to reversal, but its list is just the paths starting at A and at B. That list double-counts B-C-D-A and B-D-C-A, which are reverses of A-D-C-B and A-C-D-B. It also leaves out the two paths with endpoints C and D (C-A-B-D and C-B-A-D). Those missing paths happen not to be shorter, but B's claim to have searched everything is wrong, so its reasoning only lands on the answer by luck. A's enumeration is sound.
